newsitem.title: USA: Metagenics settles FTC ad charges.
newsitem.headline: Metagenics settles FTC ad charges.

text.p: Metagenics Inc, the maker of Ethical Nutrients brand calcium supplements, settled charges with the Federal Trade Commission on Tuesday of alleged deceptive advertising.

The FTC accused Metagenics of deceptively advertising that its Ethical Nutrients' "Bone Builder" supplements would restore bone strength, prevent bone deterioriation and osteoporosis and reduce or eliminate pain associated with bone ailments. The FTC also accused Metagenics of falsely advertising that its product was superior to similar supplements on the market.
"In this case, the company went too far in claiming that Bone Builder is superior to other sources of calcium," FTC Bureau of Consumer Protection Director Jodie Bernstein said.
To settle the charges, Metagenics, based in San Clemente, Calif., has agreed to rely upon reliable scientific evidence for its advertising.
